name: Anders Westermann
current_role: Co-owner (Westermann family) of WS Audiology via T&W Medical; former Executive Vice President of Widex
profile: Son of Widex co-founder Erik Westermann; with brother Søren and cousin Jan Tøpholm he ran Danish hearing-aid maker Widex as Executive VP. The Tøpholm and Westermann families merged Widex with Sivantos in 2019 to form WS Audiology, which they co-own with EQT via T&W Medical.
interesting_fact: Widex was founded in 1956 by Christian Tøpholm and Erik Westermann; their sons (Jan Tøpholm, Anders and Søren Westermann) later ran the company together as second-generation leaders.
notes: Very private; little recent public info. Identity of the Hurun-listed person inferred from family ownership; MarketScreener 'Anders Steen Westermann' (Widex director since 1980) may be the same person but unconfirmed. Best route likely via WS Audiology corporate communications.

name: Yen Chen Lilian
current_role: Chairwoman and Group CEO, Yulon Group (Yulon Motor), Taiwan
profile: Lilian Chen Yen (嚴陳莉蓮) is the widow of Yulon chairman Kenneth Yen (嚴凱泰), and took over leadership of Taiwan's Yulon automotive group after his death in 2018. She now steers its Nissan/Mitsubishi partnerships, EV contract manufacturing with Foxtron (Hon Hai), North American energy storage and the Yulon City mall in Xindian.
interesting_fact: In Dec 2025 Yulon sold its home-grown Luxgen brand to Foxtron (Hon Hai's EV JV) for NT$787.6m while keeping a ~43.8% stake in Foxtron.
deep_cut_fact: Before business she was a Taiwan women's national basketball player and captain of the Tai Yuen women's team; an alumna of Chinese Culture University's PE dept, she gave NT$10m in 2025 to fund scholarships and the men's basketball team there.
notes: Taiwanese, not mainland (Hurun lists 'China'). Email is Yulon Motor's spokesperson/company contact from exchange filings (spokesperson Cho Che-yu); verify on MOPS. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Clemens Toennies
current_role: Managing partner (Geschäftsführender Gesellschafter), Premium Food Group (formerly Tönnies Holding), Rheda-Wiedenbrück
profile: Trained butcher who co-founded Tönnies with brother Bernd in 1971 and built it into Germany's largest meat processor; he owns about 45%. Rebranded in 2025 as Premium Food Group (~€8bn revenue, ~22,000 staff) to diversify beyond meat, with son Max increasingly taking over management. He turned 70 in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Chaired the supervisory board of football club FC Schalke 04 from 2001 to 2020; the company HQ in Rheda-Wiedenbrück even has its own football pitch with heated turf.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he wanted to become a radio and TV mechanic rather than a butcher; he was just 15 when the company was registered with his brother and needed his parents' signature. His parents' shop processed only seven pigs a week.
notes: Press email is head of corporate communications as published in a June 2020 press release; may be outdated post-2025 rebrand. Avoid Schalke 2019-20 controversy topics. Born 27 May 1956, fifth of six children.

name: Simone Maag de Moura Cunha
current_role: Shareholder (~3.5%) of Straumann Group; no public executive role found
profile: Per Forbes, she owns about 3.5% of Swiss dental-implant maker Straumann Group. She is the niece of billionaire Rudolf Maag (Straumann's second-largest shareholder, who built Stratec Medical and merged it with Synthes) and sister-in-law of Straumann chairman-family member Thomas Straumann.
interesting_fact: Her uncle Rudolf Maag bought Straumann's medical device division in 1990, took it public as Stratec Medical, then merged it with Synthes in 1999; that stake was later sold to Johnson & Johnson.
notes: Extremely private; no independent public profile, interviews or verified accounts found. Only route is via Straumann Group corporate communications, and she has no operating role there. Low priority.

name: Andrew Brode
current_role: Non-Executive Director, RWS Holdings plc (interim Chair Jan–Oct 2026, succeeded by Patrick De Smedt)
profile: Chartered accountant who sold a family publishing business to Wolters Kluwer, bought legal journal Eclipse in 1990, and merged it with translation firm RWS in 1995, building RWS into a global AI-driven language and IP services group via acquisitions. Long-time RWS chairman and major shareholder; also a key backer/chair of Learning Technologies Group.
interesting_fact: Took over as interim chair of RWS when the chair left at end-2025, then handed over to ex-Microsoft EMEA chairman Patrick De Smedt in Oct 2026 while staying on the board.
deep_cut_fact: An Old Edwardian (left 1959), he funded half of King Edward's School Birmingham's £5m 2012 appeal and much of the school's new sports hall, named The Andrew Brode Sports Centre.
notes: Passionate mentor of young entrepreneurs (coached LTG's Jonathan Satchell, Cera's Mahiben Maruthappu) — good angle for an entrepreneurship podcast. Route via RWS company secretary or MHP.

name: Kenji Kimura
profile: Appeared once on the Forbes billionaires list (2000) with no source of wealth recorded; could not determine which Kenji Kimura this is. A Kenji Kimura is a director and former chairman of Paramount Bed Holdings (Tokyo medical-bed maker), but nothing links him to the 2000 Forbes listing.
notes: Ambiguous common name; identity not resolved. Likely a dot-com-era paper billionaire who dropped off the list after 2000. Paramount Bed link (https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/KENJI-KIMURA-A04VMT/experience) is a guess only — do not use for outreach without confirmation.

name: Hong Zhenhai
current_role: Founder and retired chairman of Eclat Textile (儒鴻, TWSE:1476), Taiwan; left the board June 2024
profile: Hung Chen-hai (洪鎮海) co-founded Eclat Textile in 1977 with NT$500,000 and built it into one of Asia's largest makers of stretch and functional fabrics and sportswear for brands like Nike. He retired in June 2024, handing the chair to Wang Shu-wen while his son became president.
interesting_fact: Known in Taiwan as the 'father of functional fabric'; Eclat reportedly never posted an annual loss in its 40+ years and became the textile sector's highest-priced stock.
deep_cut_fact: Born to a farming family in Miaoli, he started as an apprentice in a dyeing plant; after studying in Japan in the early 1980s he wove Taiwan's first roll of stretch knit fabric in 1983, and began co-developing fabrics with Nike two years later.
notes: Taiwanese (Hurun lists 'China'). Retired; publicly stated succession should be by merit not family ('傳賢不傳子'). Email is Eclat's company contact from exchange filings. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Wu Eddie Yongming
current_role: CEO and director, Alibaba Group (since Sept 2023); also leads Alibaba Cloud
profile: Eddie Wu (吴泳铭) is one of Alibaba's 18 co-founders and was its technology director at inception in 1999; his wealth stems largely from Ant Group and Alibaba stakes. After years running investments (Vision Plus Capital), he returned to succeed Daniel Zhang as CEO in 2023 and has pivoted Alibaba toward AI and cloud, with heavy capex and stakes in Moonshot, MiniMax and Zhipu.
interesting_fact: Considered Alibaba's first programmer; in 2003 he was one of seven people Jack Ma hand-picked to secretly build Taobao, and he later served as Alipay's technology director.
deep_cut_fact: His Alibaba 'flower name' (花名) is 东邪 (Dongxie, 'Eastern Heretic' from Jin Yong's novels), but colleagues affectionately call him 吴妈 ('Mama Wu'). He graduated from Zhejiang University of Technology's College of Information Engineering in 1996.
notes: Famously low-profile CEO; rarely gives interviews. Wikipedia lists Singapore citizenship. Best route via Alibaba corporate communications/IR (Head of IR Lydia Liu).

name: Andrii Verevskyi
current_role: Founder, Chairman of the Board and controlling shareholder (>95%), Kernel Holding S.A., Kyiv
profile: Born 1974 in Poltava, agronomist by training; founded a small grain-export trader in 1995 that became Kernel, Ukraine's largest sunflower-oil producer/exporter and a major grain and farming group. Took Kernel public in Warsaw in 2007, served in parliament 2002–2013, and has since bought out minorities to >95% and moved to delist.
interesting_fact: In 2012 Kernel alone accounted for about 12% of the world's sunflower-oil exports.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Kernel, he worked from 1993 to 1998 as deputy director of a regional state bread-products (khliboprodukty) enterprise; he later took a modern-economics course at Oxford (2000).
notes: Spelling varies (Verevskyi/Verevskyy/Verevskiy). Avoid the minority-shareholder delisting dispute as a topic. Gave an FT interview in 2024 on Ukraine reforms/EU, so occasionally speaks to international press.

name: Cho Hyun-beom
current_role: Chairman, Hankook & Company Group (holding company of Hankook Tire & Technology); stepped off the holding company's board in early 2026
profile: Grandson of Hankook founder Cho Hong-jai and younger son of ex-chairman Cho Yang-rai; joined Hankook Tire in 1998, rose through marketing and strategy, became CEO in 2018 and group chairman in 2021. He drove the Hanon Systems acquisition and US tire/battery expansion. After an embezzlement conviction he was paroled in mid-2026 and has begun returning to management.
interesting_fact: In 2025 he ordered that major group meetings attended by team leaders, cross-border communication and shared internal documents be conducted in English under an 'English as a Common Global Language' principle.
deep_cut_fact: Born 1972 in Haman, South Gyeongsang; he finished high school in the US and studied business at a Boston university before joining Hankook Tire's marketing side in 1998.
notes: Sensitive: convicted of embezzlement (2-year sentence, paroled ~July 2026); avoid legal and family topics. Status of formal chairman title should be rechecked. Route via Hankook corporate communications.

name: Baokun Bai
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, Guangdong KinLong Hardware Products (坚朗五金, SZSE:002791), Dongguan
profile: Bai Baokun (白宝鲲, b. 1970) founded KinLong in Dongguan in 2003 and built it into China's leading supplier of high-end door, window and curtain-wall hardware systems, listing it in Shenzhen in 2016. He remains controlling shareholder and leads the company as it expands into broader building-hardware supply.
interesting_fact: He has received a second-class National Science and Technology Progress Award and was named a 'meritorious figure' by the China Building Decoration Association.
deep_cut_fact: Besides hardware, he sits on the board of Ligao Foods (立高食品), a listed Guangzhou bakery-ingredients company; he is a trained engineer with a Peking University HSBC Business School EMBA.
notes: Low public profile; few interviews. Email is the board secretary's office (董事会办公室) per 2026 interim report. Chinese-language outreach advisable. Education details vary between sources (EMBA vs DBA).

name: Sameer Gehlaut
current_role: Founder of Spring (AI working-capital platform, New York, 2025); director/majority owner of UK challenger GB Bank; London property via family office Clivedale
profile: IIT Delhi mechanical engineer (1995) who co-founded Indiabulls in 1999 as an online brokerage with two IIT friends, growing it into housing finance (India's no.2 mortgage lender), real estate and power. He exited Indiabulls Housing (now Sammaan Capital) by 2023 and now operates from London and New York in banking, fintech and prime property.
interesting_fact: Through Clivedale he is developing the Mandarin Oriental Hotel & Residences at 22 Hanover Square, Mayfair, and in 2024 took majority control of GB Bank, which reportedly passed £2bn in retail deposits.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Rohtak, Haryana, he started Indiabulls from a small Delhi office and won the Ernst & Young Entrepreneur of the Year award in 2006, two years after the IPO.
notes: Clivedale email is the company's general enquiries address (his London property vehicle). Avoid regulatory/legal topics (Yes Bank, EOW FIR Dec 2025). Fintech/AI angle (Spring) fits an entrepreneurship podcast. Recent coverage is largely sponsored PR.
